subject: Mid-cycle reconciliation: multiplexed ingest counts and provisional credit
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightcart.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@brightcart.com
Date: 2028-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midcycle counts — sharp surge Mar 19-20 looks doubled?

Hi Michael,

We flagged an unexpected spike in our March 19-20 usage that appears to have been double-attributed to two parallel ingest streams (staging and production). The invoice posted today includes ~1.2M extra tokens compared to our internal telemetry.

Quick summary:
- Our own logs show the client shipped a single batch of requests at 03/19 18:04 UTC.
- Your portal shows two ingestion groups with identical request_ids during the same minute.
- The net impact on our March invoice (gross) is $12,340 and, critically for us, an increase in VAT charged for our EU entity.

Can you: 1) confirm whether Redwood observed duplicate request ingestion across a short-lived multiplexer; 2) share the per-request export for 03/19-03/20; and 3) advise on a provisional credit path while you investigate (we need to present a corrected P&L to our CFO tomorrow).

I've attached a small zip with our internal trace (brightcart_evidence.zip). Please loop in billing/tax as needed.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround on this.

—Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Integrations, BrightCart
oliver@brightcart.com
+1 415-555-0122

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midcycle counts — sharp surge Mar 19-20 looks doubled?

Hi Oliver — thanks for the heads up and for the evidence. Sorry for the trouble here.

Ben (billing) and Kimberly (tax) are copied — Ben will pull the per-request export and look for identical request_id fingerprints across groups; Kimberly will confirm VAT treatment if this is a retroactive adjustment.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to attach a raw usage export for 03/19 00:00 UTC — 03/20 23:59 UTC showing request_id, stream_id, route, and tokens_consumed.
- If we confirm duplication, Redwood will issue a provisional credit for the overage (gross), and Kimberly will provide guidance on VAT reversal vs. credit memo for BrightCart's EU entity.
- We will provide an explanation note you can share with your CFO and, if helpful, a short walk-through call today at 3pm PT.

Oliver — can you confirm whether the affected payments are already in collections or if you prefer a credit applied to the next invoice?

Attaching our internal ticket: HC-98765 (we'll keep you updated in-thread).

Best,
Mike
Michael Grant
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Midcycle counts — raw export + suggested provisional credit

Mike / Kim — I pulled the raw token export for BrightCart for 2028-03-19 00:00 — 2028-03-20 23:59 UTC. Attach: usage_export_Mar2028.csv (CSV stub: request_id, timestamp_utc, stream_id, tokens).

Summary of what I found: 
- 1,201,732 tokens appear twice with matching request_ids across stream_id "prod-eu-1" and "stg-eu-2" within a 60s window (same client_id, same user_agent).
- The duplicated window is ~18:04 — 18:07 UTC on 2028-03-19.
- No other accounts in that time window show similar duplication, suggesting this was specific to BrightCart's routing pattern + a short multiplexer race condition we rolled out on 2028-03-19 18:03:05 UTC.

Recommendation: provisional gross credit = $12,340.00 (we calculate using your ratecard tier for March).
Operational notes:
- I'll mark the ticket HC-98765 with the raw export and a pointer to the commit that introduced the mux rollback.
- We should not apply this credit until tax treatment is confirmed. Kimberly, any guidance on VAT reversal vs. issuing a credit note? If we issue a credit note we need to include the original invoice number and specify reversed VAT so BrightCart can reclaim.

Ben
Ben Carter
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Midcycle counts — resolution plan and provisional credit (BrightCart)

Hi Oliver — quick update and next steps.

1) Root cause: our rollout introduced a short-lived multiplexer that, in a small percentage of cases, forwarded the same request to two ingest groups. Ben's export confirms duplicated request_ids for the window you flagged.

2) Credit: Redwood will issue a provisional gross credit of $12,340.00 against invoice #2028-03-19 once we have confirmation on VAT handling.

3) VAT treatment: Kimberly confirms the preferred path is a credit note referencing the original invoice so BrightCart's EU entity can reclaim VAT. Kimberly: please provide the credit note template and the reversal VAT line we should include.

4) Collections/payment: Oliver — we can either apply the credit to your next invoice (fast) or refund the paid amount and issue a corrected invoice + credit note (slower). Which do you prefer?

5) Evidence package: attaching usage_export_Mar2028.csv and the internal ticket link for audit. For your records we've also created a DocuSign approval link for the credit note: https://docusign.com/REDWOOD/credit-approval/DC-7831 (please sign if you'd like the refund route).

If you want, Ben and I can join a short 20-minute call tomorrow to walk your finance team through the export. Thanks again for raising this — we'll make it right.

Best,
Mike
Michael Grant
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com
